data: The only suit worn on Soyuz — created after the Soyuz 11 decompression deaths in 1971
Soft pressure suit worn inside the Soyuz descent module on every launch and re-entry since 1980 (the Sokol-K family since 1973). Back-entry seam, fixed helmet, umbilical-fed life support.
The Soyuz launch-entry suit, mandatory since the 1971 Soyuz 11 decompression deaths

Soft pressure suit worn inside the Soyuz descent module on every launch and re-entry since Soyuz T-2 in 1980, replacing the original Sokol-K. Back-entry seam (laced shut), fixed helmet with flip-up visor, umbilical for O₂ + comms + cooling water. Not designed for spacewalking — it is the backup that keeps the crew alive long enough to land if cabin pressure fails.
The latest of a 50-year line of Russian rear-entry EVA suits
The Soviet lunar suit that never flew — its DNA lives in every Orlan and Feitian
The white US spacewalk suit — every American EVA from the Shuttle to the ISS
The J-mission suit — added a waist joint so astronauts could sit in the Lunar Rover
The first operational lunar surface suit — Apollo 11 through 14
Sokol KV-2 suit worn by Tim Peake on Soyuz TMA-19M (2015–2016)
